title: One Idea, Five Posts: A Simple Repurposing Framework
content:
Most content creators burn out chasing new ideas when the real bottleneck isn't ideas — it's formats. One good idea can fuel a week of content if you know how to reshape it.

The framework

1. The core insight. Write the idea in one or two sentences. This becomes your anchor post — a short, punchy statement of the idea.

2. The explainer. Take that same idea and unpack it into a longer post with context, an example, and a takeaway.

3. The list. Break the idea into 3–5 concrete steps or examples. Lists perform well because they're scannable and easy to save.

4. The question. Flip the idea into a question for your audience. Questions drive comments, and comments drive reach.

5. The visual. Turn the core insight into a simple graphic, quote card, or short video script.

Why this works

You're not repeating yourself — you're meeting your audience where they already are. Some people only skim headlines, some only read long-form, some only engage with visuals. One idea, reshaped five ways, reaches all of them without doubling your workload.
